Plot MODGEE result

Source: R/plot_modgee.R
plot_modgee.Rd

Visualize cumulative extinction, species extinction probabilities, or conditional expected extinction years from an existing MODGEE fit.

Usage

plot_modgee(result, type = "curve")

Arguments

result

A result list returned by fit_modgee() using the current output format. Older objects must be refitted or updated to that format.

type

A single string: "curve" (default), "probability", or "time". Full names are required.

Value

A ggplot object. The function neither saves a file nor explicitly prints the plot. Use print() inside loops and ggplot2::ggsave() to save it.

Details

All plots use a white background, a closed black panel border, no grid, larger axis text, and a two-column legend below the panel. Groups use green, orange, blue and purple first; additional groups extend the palette.

Cumulative extinction curves

type = "curve" plots result$curve$time against result$curve$cumulative_extinction_rate. The axes are labelled Year and Cumulative extinction rate. Rates are shown as percentages. The overall curve is a thick black line. For grouped fits, coloured group curves from result$group_results$curve are also shown, and the overall curve is labelled Overall in the legend. The fitted overall curve is used directly, not an unweighted average of group curves. No smoothing is added. When bootstrap intervals are available, a grey band shows the overall pointwise confidence interval from result$bootstrap$curve, at the confidence level used in fitting. Group curves retain their original colours without additional bands. Missing interval bounds leave gaps in the band.

Extinction probability histograms

type = "probability" counts recorded species using result$species$p_extinct. Bins have width 0.1, with boundaries [0, 0.1], (0.1, 0.2], ..., (0.9, 1]. The axes are Extinction probability and Number of species. Grouped fits use stacked colours, so each bar's total is the total number of species in that interval. Counts are not normalized by group size.

Expected extinction years

type = "time" plots estimated_extinction_year against p_extinct, with one point per eligible species. The axes are Expected extinction year and Extinction probability. Estimated years are conditional means given extinction, not confirmed extinction dates. They are read directly from the species table and are already mapped to the numeric time labels supplied during fitting. If interval indices were supplied instead of years, the plot retains those indices despite the default year labels; labels can be changed with ggplot2::labs(). No jitter or regression line is added.

Groups and missing estimates

Group membership comes from result$species$belonged_group. Group order and the colour mapping use result$group_results$summary. The same group has the same colour across the three plot types. All-zero species are excluded from species-level plots. Groups containing only all-zero species have no fitted curve and no recorded species to plot. Dark extinction estimates are not converted into artificial species records.

For probability histograms, missing or non-finite estimates are omitted with a warning giving their count. Time plots silently omit species with missing or non-finite estimates or zero extinction probability, because their conditional extinction time is undefined. Missing curve estimates, unknown groups, duplicate species identifiers, invalid probabilities, or no eligible observations result in an error. Only the fields needed by the requested plot are required.

Usage Examples


plot_modgee(example_result)
plot_modgee(example_result, type = "probability")
plot_modgee(example_result, type = "time")

plot_modgee(example_grouped_result)
plot_modgee(example_grouped_result, type = "probability")
plot_modgee(example_grouped_result, type = "time")

# Precomputed bootstrap fit with an overall confidence band.
plot_modgee(example_bootstrap_result)

# Save a plot to a PNG file.
p <- plot_modgee(example_bootstrap_result)
ggplot2::ggsave("modgee_curve.png", plot = p,
                width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 300)
